描述_ZN: The Qianlong Imperial Ode to the Five Blessings, Qing dynasty, inscribed in majestic regular script, 14 cm long and 26.6 cm wide. This is an 8-panel scroll.　　This panel is signed "Respectfully written by Zichen Yong Yan", with inscriptions of "Zichen Yong Yan" in white and "Respectfully written" in vermilion.　　Yong Yan was the fifteenth son of Emperor Jiaqing, Emperor Gaozong of the Qing Dynasty, and the fifteenth son of Emperor Qianlong of the Qing Dynasty. In the thirty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign (1773) was secretly established as the Crown Prince. Qianlong sixty years (1795) in September, was formally established as the Crown Prince. The first day of the first month of the following year, by the Qianlong emperor within the Zen, that is, the emperor's throne, the year named Jiaqing.　　This volume contains the full text and preface of the "Ode to the Five Blessings" written by the Qianlong emperor in 1776, which is published in volume 37 of the Qianlong Emperor's Second Collection of Imperial Texts. The five blessings refer to longevity, wealth, health and tranquility, good virtue, and final life. The Qianlong emperor elaborated on each of these according to the Confucian classics, and believed that longevity, wealth, health and tranquility and final life were granted by heaven and could not be forced, but only "Youhao De" could be achieved by human beings, so he paid special attention to "cultivating virtue" in order to pray for others.
